messages:
sara: Unexpected KMS hiccup last night in us-west-2 caused some jump-hosts to switch to a local fallback keystore. We didn't have ephemeral RBAC bindings in place so ops had to use broader permissions. Drafting mitigation + audit checklist.

kevin: we need the minimum privilege plan asap. no clusterRole please.

anna: minimal: namespace-scoped SA + Role granting keystore.get/update and secrets.patch for jump-hosts namespace. RoleBinding should be ephemeral with TTL (60m). Use annotations to record operator.

mike: canary owner volunteers? i can run if scripted. also want to ensure we keep strong audit slices for SOC.

ops-bot: Alert: KMS degraded 2026-03-22T23:12Z -> 23:19Z (us-west-2). 503 spike observed.

sara: mitigation steps (draft): 1) create SA fallback-ops in jump-hosts; 2) apply Role + ephemeral RoleBinding; 3) deploy local-keystore secret to jumphosts; 4) enable keystore plugin audit + kube-audit verbose; 5) run 2-host canary; 6) rotate fallback keys and revoke cached tokens.

dave: small ops note: ensure jumphost code honors RETRY_BACKOFF to avoid flip-flopping between KMS/local. suggest backoff config: 200ms base, max attempts 6.

ellie: SOC needs correlation fields: request_id, host_id, service_account, cosign_sig_id. add to runbook outputs.

anna: binding script sketch (to be committed via gitops PR):
```
kubectl -n jump-hosts create sa fallback-ops
kubectl -n jump-hosts apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: keystore-operator
rules:
- apiGroups: ["keystore.internal.redwood.io"]
  resources: ["keystores","keys"]
  verbs: ["get","update","patch"]
EOF
# create RoleBinding with annotation and TTL enforced by controller
kubectl -n jump-hosts create rolebinding fallback-keystore-ops --role=keystore-operator --serviceaccount=jump-hosts:fallback-ops --annotation=\"created-by=runbook/sara\"
```

kevin: audit export plan: collect kube-audit logs + keystore plugin logs between 23:00-23:30Z, gzip, encrypt with SSE-KMS, and upload to s3://redwood-soc-archives/kms-incidents/INC-2026-03122/. I'll own upload.

sara: runbook link (draft): https://internal.redwood/sops/runbooks/keystore-fallback-ephemeral - includes test commands. Pasting quick test steps in thread.

sara: ```bash
# apply local-keystore secret
kubectl -n jump-hosts create secret generic local-keystore --from-file=keystore.json=./keystore.json --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
# enable fallback env
kubectl -n jump-hosts set env daemon/jumphost FALLBACK_KS=local --record
# note: --record will save command in resource annotation for auditing
```

kevin: question: rotate fallback keys? compliance will want rotation + attestation.

sara: yes. runbook step: rotate local keystore keys after successful canary and run cosign re-attestations for any rebuilt host images. add revoke step for cached tokens.

mike: i'll run canary tomorrow 09:30 PT; anna please finish binding PR. also add metrics: keystore.fallback.count and keystore.fallback.latency_ms and an alert: keystore.fallback.count > 5 in 5m -> pager.

ellie: SOC will triage after canary. i'll need the exported logs and the binding PR link. also require that any operator who created the binding includes `--record` and a link to their PR for compliance.

anna: i'll implement a small controller to garbage-collect RoleBindings after TTL, and add annotation requirement `created-by` + `operator-email`. PR template will include reason, TTL, operator, and rollback steps.

ops-bot: Reminder: create incident INC-2026-03122 and tag teams.

sara: owners: anna -> binding PR & controller, mike -> canary run, kevin -> audit export & s3 upload, ellie -> SOC triage & artifacts, dave -> retry/backoff config review. I'll update the runbook and cut the gitops PRs. Closing when PRs merged.
